memory_update.text: NNI is the strongest public reference anchor for student-loan servicing and education payment rails; keep for Layer 2 evidence checks on servicing volume, contract economics, borrower counts, and segment margin.
FLYW is an underfollowed second-order candidate: not a Title IV vendor, but its education payment, reconciliation, collections, and student financial software may act as bursar/audit infrastructure.

LOPE should be tracked as an outsourced regulated-operations platform for university partners, with special attention to financial aid, return-to-Title-IV, state authorization, accreditation, and partner concentration.

Pure-play Title IV compliance, accreditation workflow, and state authorization software vendors found in search appear mostly private; public exposure likely hides in broader education services, payments, loan servicing, regtech, or government-services companies.

summary: Expanded one regulatory-infrastructure node inside the Education theme. The strongest public-market mapping is not pure-play Title IV compliance software, because many purpose-built vendors appear private. The investable lane therefore maps to adjacent rails: student-loan servicing systems, education payment/reconciliation infrastructure, outsourced university services that touch financial aid and compliance, and legacy education-loan portfolios. This pass identifies one reference anchor and three underfollowed or speculative-shadow names for later evidence testing.
